text: Then there is a problem with the most famous version of this theory. Abel claimed that the philosopher Em-peddokleez reported finding such bones on Sicily. Later researchers have found no surviving ancient source that says so. The palaeontologist Mark Witton and Richard Hing put it bluntly: without that story, they argue, the idea becomes baseless. Elephant fossils and one-eyed monsters turn up all over the world, and no ancient text or artwork makes the Sicilian link stand out. The scholars of Greek myth Mercedes Ah-gheereh and Richard Buxton make a similar point. Theories like this sound plausible, they say, but lack a chain of argument linking origin to myth.
